name: BlockKeywords
description: Blocks messages containing specific user-defined keywords, as if the user sending them was blocked.
summary: Hides messages containing words or patterns you choose

settings.label: Blocked words
settings.description: Comma-separated list of words to block

settings.label: Use regex
settings.description: Use each value as a regular expression when checking message content (advanced)

settings.label: Regex Helper
settings.description: Test your regular expressions against a sample input

settings.label: Case sensitive
settings.description: Whether to use a case sensitive search or not

notes: Messages whose text, or an embed's title or description, contains one of your comma-separated words (as a whole word, case-insensitive unless "Case sensitive" is on) are hidden from the chat, and so don't count as unread or notify. With "Use regex" each entry is a regular expression instead; commas inside [...] and {n,m} stay part of the pattern, as upstream. Regex Helper asks for a sample text and lists each pattern as matching (✓), not matching (✗) or invalid (⚠, with the reason). Changes apply at once, without upstream's restart. As upstream, a word that starts or ends with a symbol (such as c++) never matches, as whole-word matching needs letters or digits at its edges.
gaps: Qord has no collapsed "blocked message" row: matching messages are hidden outright, as NoBlockedMessages hides blocked users' messages.
Hidden messages never count as unread, so "Ignore blocked messages" off has no effect.
An invalid regular expression is skipped instead of stopping the plugin; Regex Helper shows why it is invalid.
Patterns are Qt (PCRE2) regular expressions, which match JavaScript's for everyday patterns.
